title: Observe and Refresh: automated drift detection for performance profiles
creator: Nina Patel
description: Problem statement: Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency/throughput/cost) are published during model onboarding and when new model versions are verified. Over time, runtime changes, kernel swaps, dataset drift, or hidden hardware behavior can cause actual production characteristics to diverge from the published profile. We need an automated way to detect drift in profile metrics, re-run verification tests on affected model pins, and either refresh the published profile or flag human review and (if needed) rollback model-pin changes. Goal: reduce silent regressions, shorten time-to-detect, and make profile maintenance low-touch for teams running at scale.
background: Current flow: profiles are published by the verification pipeline and signed into the registry. There is no continuous monitoring that compares live observed token-level latency/cost/throughput distributions to the profile baselines. Ops and platform teams surface issues via dashboards and incidents, but detection is manual and often tied to customer reports or QA runs. Existing related work: PM-7120 (deprecation policy), PM-10234 (profile release contract) — these are dependencies for safe rollback semantics.
proposal:
Introduce an Observe+Refresh subsystem with three capabilities:

1) Continuous profile health metrics: emit aggregated profile-level stats from the runtime and Console (per-model-pin): p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/sec (throughput), per-request cost estimate. Metrics are ingested into a profiles-health index with retention and comparison windows.

2) Drift detection engine: a scheduled job that compares recent distributions to the verification baseline using statistical tests (e.g., KS-test for latency distributions, Poisson confidence intervals for throughput). Use configurable thresholds (relative and absolute) and an alert scoring model that accounts for traffic volume and anomaly persistence.

3) Automated re-verify + refresh workflow: when a profile is flagged, trigger the verification pipeline on representative synthetic workload and a sampled production replay. If the verification run reproduces the drift (failing defined acceptance criteria), create a refresh PR for the profile registry and optionally mark it for auto-publish depending on policy. If the refreshed profile causes regression compared to prior guardrails, generate a rollback recommendation for model-pin changes and notify the owner. All events are auditable in Console and recorded in the profile registry.
scope: MVP: metrics emission + drift detector + automated verification trigger and console flags. Exclude automatic rollback in MVP (will require additional guardrails and legal/compliance review). Integrations: runtime metrics, Console dashboards, verification pipeline, profile registry.
success_metrics: Time-to-detect median for profile regressions reduced from ~3 days to <6 hours
False positive rate of automated flags under 10% after calibration
>80% of flagged profiles result in either automated refresh or human-reviewed PR within 48 hours
Reduction in customer-facing incidents attributable to unnoticed profile drift by 60% over 6 months
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits profile-level aggregated metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput tokens/sec, cost estimates) for pinned model versions to the profiles-health index
Drift detector job runs on schedule and produces reproducible alerts in Console for a seeded set of synthetic anomalies
Verification pipeline can be triggered programmatically by the drift system and returns structured pass/fail + metrics summary
Flagged profiles generate an audit entry in the registry and a Console ticket with suggested next steps
Documentation updated: profile health dashboard, runbook for review/refresh, and owner notification flow
rollout_plan: 1) Instrumentation: small runtime change to tag emitted metrics and wire into profiles-health (canary 10% of traffic). 2) Drift detector in staging, run against historical data to calibrate thresholds. 3) Enable in production in monitoring-only mode for 1 week (no PRs created). 4) Enable auto-triggered verification (no auto-publish) and expose flags in Console to owners. 5) After 4 weeks of telemetry and tuning, evaluate auto-publish gates for low-risk model families.

Eng (runtime): add profile-level metric tags and emit aggregation keys
Eng (infra): create profiles-health index and retention policy in observability stack
Eng (verification): add API to programmatically trigger verification runs and return structured summaries
Eng (automations): implement drift detector service and alert scoring
Design: Console flags and profile health view (mockups + accessibility review)
SRE: runbook and incident playbook updates
Docs: developer guide and runbook for profile refresh flow
risks: False positives causing unnecessary churn and developer fatigue
Instrumenting metrics at high-cardinality could increase telemetry costs
Automated verification may not reproduce production variance leading to noisy signals
Rollback/autopublish without human review could cause regressions in output quality or customer impact
mitigations: Start in monitoring-only mode; require human approval for first X refreshes
Throttle and sample metrics to bound observability costs; use aggregated windows
Include production replay and seeded synthetic tests in verification runs to improve reproducibility
Add governance: policy matrix that restricts auto-publish to vetted model families and capacity tiers
notes: Design discussion 2025-01-20: prefer KS-test for latency distribution comparisons and a minimum traffic floor (10k tokens over comparison window) before evaluating. Engineering prefers a sidecar metrics emitter to avoid widespread model/runtime changes. We will reuse the verification pipeline's existing job runner to avoid duplication.
